caption: A strip of tissue paper is held above a hot radiator, and it lifts and flutters upward in the warm air.

sa.check: A strip of tissue paper is held above a radiator.
The strip is held above the radiator, not beside it.

pc.expect: The strip lifts and dances only while it is over the radiator and hangs still when held away from it.
pc.fail: The strip flutters while held well away from the radiator with nothing else moving; or the strip hangs dead still directly over the radiator; or the strip flutters before it is brought over the radiator; or the strip keeps dancing after it has been taken away and held elsewhere.

pc.expect: Over the radiator the strip is carried upward and its free end rises; away from it the strip hangs downward.
pc.fail: The strip hangs straight down while directly over the radiator; or the strip is pushed downward toward the radiator; or the strip lifts while held below the radiator; or the strip stands out stiffly sideways with nothing blowing it.

pc.expect: The strip is a limp light sheet that ripples along its length and folds over.
pc.fail: The strip stays a rigid flat board as it rises; or stretches as it lifts; or holds a fixed wave shape frozen in place; or stands stiff like a wire.

pc.expect: Other light things in the rising air over the radiator stir too, and the strip's flutter is strongest where the air leaves the radiator.
pc.fail: The strip flutters hard while dust or a curtain right beside it hangs dead still; or the flutter is strongest far out to the side of the radiator; or the strip stirs while nothing else in the rising air does.
pc.precondition: Other light items such as dust, a curtain or a second strip are in the rising air.

pc.expect: One strip; it stays one piece and does not pass through the radiator.
pc.fail: The strip vanishes; or a second strip appears; or the strip passes through the radiator's fins; or the strip merges with the curtain.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The radiator's paint, the wall and the room stay the same.
pc.fail: The radiator changes colour; or the wall changes colour; or items in the room rearrange.

note: Whoever holds the strip is not judged.
